```yaml
name: Clean Unused L10n Strings

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 0 1 * *'          # Monthly at midnight UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

jobs:
  check-unused-strings:
    name: Check for unused L10n strings
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'

      - name: Install jq
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq

      - name: Detect unused strings
        id: detect
        run: |
          python Tools/detect_unused_strings.py > unused.json
          COUNT=$(jq -r '.count' unused.json)
          echo "unused_count=$COUNT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "unused_json<<EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          cat unused.json >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Post comment if unused strings found
        if: steps.detect.outputs.unused_count != '0'
        uses: peter-evans/create-or-update-comment@v4
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          issue-number: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          body: |
            ⚠️ **Unused L10n strings detected** ⚠️
            Found **${{ steps.detect.outputs.unused_count }}** unused L10n strings.
            Details:
            ```json
            ${{ steps.detect.outputs.unused_json }}
            ```

  clean-unused-strings:
    name: Clean unused L10n strings
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'

      - name: Install jq
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq

      - name: Detect unused strings
        id: detect
        run: |
          python Tools/detect_unused_strings.py > unused.json
          COUNT=$(jq -r '.count' unused.json)
          echo "unused_count=$COUNT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "unused_json<<EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          cat unused.json >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Remove unused strings
        if: steps.detect.outputs.unused_count != '0'
        run: |
          python Tools/remove_unused_strings.py unused.json

      - name: Commit changes
        if: steps.detect.outputs.unused_count != '0'
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add .
          git commit -m "chore: remove ${{ steps.detect.outputs.unused_count }} unused L10n strings"
          git push origin HEAD:cleanup-unused-strings-${{ github.run_id }}

      - name: Create pull request
        if: steps.detect.outputs.unused_count != '0'
        uses: peter-evans/create-pull-request@v6
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          title: "chore: remove ${{ steps.detect.outputs.unused_count }} unused L10n strings"
          body: |
            This PR removes ${{ steps.detect.outputs.unused_count }} unused L10n strings detected by the automated workflow.
            Details:
            ```json
            ${{ steps.detect.outputs.unused_json }}
            ```
          branch: cleanup-unused-strings-${{ github.run_id }}
          base: main
          delete-branch: true
```
